title: Silver, We Have a Problem (and investors are missing it) | Jeff Christian
speaker: Jeffrey Christian (CPM Group)

macro_themes.view: Inflation persistent (PCE 3.4%, core 3%); expects possibly one more 25bp hike, not four.
Q4 2026/early 2027 budget-bill spending cuts after the midterms could push the US into recession; timing unknowable; yield curve is not a useful predictor.
10y ~5% is rising for bad reasons (deficits, credit-dependent consumers); real rates ~1.5-2% are below the ~3% level that historically hurts gold.
Dollar very strong and foreign Treasury holdings at record; de-dollarisation narrative overstated.
~90% of gold's rising reserve share is price, only ~10% buying; buying narrative exaggerated.
Top-heavy market driven by AI/crypto/data centres; a sharp decline is possible.
Risks greatest since December 1941; hold gold, silver and cash as no-counterparty assets.

calls.reason: Expects midterm-election and world risks to drive gold buying into late November (Dec butterfly calls); for a 3-5 year hold buy a leveraged gold ETF; positive real rates still below 3% trigger.
calls.quote: predicated on the idea that the US congressional elections are going to cause investors to buy a lot of gold and push the price up

calls.reason: Fabrication demand down ~5% and solar demand down ~10% this year (thrifting, copper substitution, overcapacity) and investors selling bar/coin; but still recommends adding gold and silver as protection.
calls.quote: we have solar demand falling about 10% this year and we have uh total uh fabrication demand for silver falling about 5% this year

calls.reason: CPM sees persistent and growing surpluses as mine output recovers and fabrication demand falls, which explains the drop from January record highs; WPIC deficits inflated by counting investment demand.
calls.quote: you have a much bigger surplus once again, which fully explains the decline in platinum from record highs in January

calls.reason: Market tight short and long term; Centinela strike threat (as soon as Oct 13) cuts supply and drives investment buying of futures.
calls.quote: The copper market is relatively tight both on a short-term and a long-term basis.

calls.reason: Sells part of USO: oil could decline on speculative selling if Strait of Hormuz situation doesn't deteriorate further.
calls.quote: I do think that the oil prices perhaps potentially could decline.

calls.reason: Sells the Bitcoin-treasury holding: dislikes assets that 'sound like a scam' and lack a recoverable counterparty.
calls.quote: I just don't like things that sound like a scam to me

calls.reason: Top-heavy market reliant on AI/crypto/data centres; sharp decline possible alongside recession.
calls.quote: So you could see a sharp decline in the stock market.

notes: Host: 'week ending the 4th of October 2026'; PCE referred to as 'yesterday', so likely recorded Oct 3 (weekend). Title says 'Silver, we have a problem' but silver view is demand-weak rather than an explicit price call; SI medium 'mixed' reflects that plus his buy-metals-for-protection advice. ES/BTC calls are low-conviction inferences from his general bearish/sceptical comments. TNX: no directional yield forecast beyond 'rising for bad reasons' (themes only). Expects another 25bp Fed hike possible.
